caption:
اردو شاعری تشبیہ، کنایہ اور استعارہ کے وسیع  و عمدہ  استعمال کے حوالے سے جانی جاتی ہے۔  ہم آپ کو اس نظم کے ذریعے ایسی ایک مثال سے متعارف کرواتے ہیں۔گُُل اور بلبل، جس میں  عاشق کی تشبیہ بلبل ، اور معشوق کی تشبیہ گل سے دی گئی ہے ۔ 

اس شعر میں شاعر محبوب کے لیے اپنی محبت کا موازنہ  بلبل کی گل سے محبت سے کرتا ہے ۔

Urdu poetry is known for its rich use of similes, metaphors, and symbolism. Through this poem we’ll introduce you to one such example: the gul (rose) and bulbul (nightingale) where the latter  represents the lover, and the rose represents the beloved. 

In the couplet, the poet compares the love that he has for his beloved to the sincere love of the nightingale for the rose. See our newsletter for a link to a paper to explore the imagery some more!
.
.
.

Piyam-e-Iqbal: Join us in conversation with Zirrar Ali on the poetry, legacy and philosophy of Allama Iqbal, followed by a Q&A.

پیامِ اقبال: ‎آئیے اقبال کی شاعری، فلسفے، اور ‎میراث سے متعلق گفتگو کے لئے شامل ہوں ضرار علی کے ساتھ! آپ کے پاس سوالات پوچھنے اور ضرار کی کتاب غازی و گلستان خریدنے کا موقع بھی ہوگا!

The event will take place in the Sidgwick Hall at Newnham College. 
.
.
.
The discussion will be followed by an opportunity to purchase Zirrar’s latest book ‘Ghazi and the Garden’, a modern translation of Iqbal’s poetry. ‘Considered by many to be the last of the great classical Persian poets, and among the first modern Muslim philosophers, Iqbal’s work has been pivotal in anti-colonial movements and revolutions throughout the Muslim world in the 20th century. Though he is a household name in the Indian subcontinent, Iran and Turkey, this translation is highly valuable to English readers. This collection brings together some of his most poignant and powerful Urdu poems taken from Bang-e Dra (Call of the Marching Bell) and Bal-e Jibreel (Gabriel’s Wing), as well as some of his finest Persian ghazals from Zabur-e Ajam (Persian Psalms).’

caption:
!خوش آمدید 

Welcome to Cambridge University Urdu Society! This is a platform for anyone with an appreciation of Urdu language, adab (literature) or shayari (poetry) to benefit from the rich literature which has been made foreign for us.

So whether you're a well versed poet, just discovering the wise words of Iqbal, or simply miss hearing Urdu while at Cambridge, this is the society for you! All levels of Urdu speakers are welcome and we aspire to make our events as inclusive as possible :)

We look forward to hosting speaker events, reading circles, socials and so much more! 

Follow us and watch this space for more updates coming soon!
.
.
.

Why she joined the Committee: 
‘The language of love, urdu zabaan is an open call for a 'bazm' of lovers, those who have failed in love or are in love, finding love. The way, and all the meanings held within it, that it embraces the person in frenzy makes it all the more attractive for one to not love this language. Hence, the lost self is also trying to find meaning in the midst of chaos and desolation.’
